hindi: अब इसके बाद हम 'नवेगान्धारणीय' नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called "Navegāndhāraṇīya" (On Not Suppressing the Urges).
notes: Prose opening formula, not a verse (the unit is typed as "verse"). The chapter name is a taddhita formed from the opening words na vegān dhārayet (7.3).

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा था।
english: Thus spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula, not a verse. sma with āha gives a past sense.

hindi: बुद्धिमान् व्यक्ति उत्पन्न हुए मूत्र और पुरीष के वेगों को न रोके, न शुक्र के, न वात के, न छर्दि के और न छींक के।
english: The wise one should not suppress the urges of urine and faeces when they have arisen, nor of semen, nor of flatus (vāta), nor of vomiting, nor of sneezing;
notes: The list of urges continues in 7.4. vāta here is the downward wind (flatus), not the doṣa in general.
lines_deva: न रेतसो न वातस्य न छर्द्याः क्षवथोर्न च
lines_iast: na retaso na vātasya na chardyāḥ kṣavathorna ca

hindi: न डकार के, न जम्भाई के, न भूख और प्यास के वेगों को, न आँसुओं के, न निद्रा के और न श्रम से होने वाले श्वास के।
english: nor of belching, nor of yawning, nor the urges of hunger and thirst, nor of tears, nor of sleep, nor of breathing due to exertion.

text_flags.why: Printed nā (twice in this verse) gives no sense; the negative na is required by the series and gives the regular 16-syllable half-verse either way; probably a typing slip.

notes: Continues the sentence of 7.3. niḥśvāsasya śrameṇa: the breathing that comes from exertion.
lines_deva: नोद्गारस्य न जृम्भाया ना वेगान् क्षुत्पिपासयोः
ना बाष्पस्य न निद्राया निःश्वासस्य श्रमेण च
lines_iast: nodgārasya na jṛmbhāyā nā vegān kṣutpipāsayoḥ
nā bāṣpasya na nidrāyā niḥśvāsasya śrameṇa ca

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. √dhṛ
m. gen. sg. pres. part. ni-√gad

hindi: इन उत्पन्न हुए वेगों को रोकने वाले को जो रोग होते हैं, उन्हें चिकित्सा के लिए अलग-अलग कहते हुए मुझसे सुनो।
english: Hear from me, as I tell them one by one for the sake of treatment, the diseases that arise in one who suppresses these urges when they have arisen.
notes: me nigadataḥ: genitive of the speaker with śṛṇu ("hear from me as I speak").
lines_deva: एतान् धारयतो जातान् वेगान् रोगा भवन्ति ये
lines_iast: etān dhārayato jātān vegān rogā bhavanti ye

hindi: मूत्र के वेग को रोकने पर बस्ति और मेहन में शूल, मूत्रकृच्छ्र, सिरदर्द, विनाम और वंक्षण में आनाह — ये लक्षण होते हैं।
english: Pain in the bladder and penis, difficult urination (mūtrakṛcchra), headache, bending of the body (vināma) and distension of the groins would be the signs when urine is suppressed.
notes: śirorujā: rujā as a feminine noun "pain". liṅgam is singular in the text, rendered "signs" for the list. mūtrakṛcchra is usually equated with dysuria (standard). vaṃkṣaṇa printed with anusvāra, restored as vaṅkṣaṇa.

hindi: मूत्र के रुकने पर स्वेद, अवगाहन, अभ्यंग, घृत का अवपीडक और तीन प्रकार का बस्तिकर्म करना चाहिए।
english: When urine is obstructed one should apply sweating, immersion baths, oil massage, the avapīḍaka of ghee and the threefold enema therapy (basti).
notes: avapīḍaka: a dose of ghee; commentators (Cakrapāṇi) explain it as ghee taken before and after a meal. The three kinds of basti are not named in the verse; commentators take them as nirūha, anuvāsana and uttara-basti.

words.gram: n. loc. sg. ppp. caus. vi-√dhṛ

hindi: पुरीष के वेग को रोकने पर पक्वाशय और सिर में शूल, वायु और मल का न निकलना, पिण्डलियों में ऐंठन और आध्मान होते हैं।
english: Pain in the colon (pakvāśaya) and head, non-passage of flatus and faeces, cramping of the calves and distension (ādhmāna) would occur when faeces is suppressed.
notes: pakvāśaya: the receptacle of digested matter, usually taken as the colon (standard). ādhmāna: abdominal distension with gas.

hindi: मल के रुकने पर स्वेद, अभ्यंग, अवगाहन, वर्तियाँ, बस्तिकर्म और प्रमाथी अन्नपान हितकर हैं।
english: When faeces is obstructed, sweating, oil massage, immersion baths, suppositories (varti), enema therapy and food and drink that is pramāthin are beneficial.
notes: varti literally "wick"; here the rectal suppository. pramāthin: a drug or food that drastically clears matter accumulated in the channels; not glossed further in this verse. hitam is singular, agreeing with the nearest item.

hindi: शुक्र के रुकने पर मेढ्र और वृषणों में शूल, अंगमर्द, हृदय में व्यथा और मूत्र का रुकना भी होता है।
english: When semen is obstructed there would be pain in the penis and testicles, body-ache, distress in the heart, and obstructed urine as well.
notes: hṛdi may mean the heart or the chest region.
lines_deva: भवेत् प्रतिहते शुक्रे विबद्धं मूत्रमेव च
lines_iast: bhavet pratihate śukre vibaddhaṃ mūtrameva ca

hindi: वहाँ अभ्यंग, अवगाहन, मदिरा, चरणायुध, शालि, दूध, निरूह और मैथुन भी प्रशस्त हैं।
english: There, oil massage, immersion bath, wine (madirā), cocks (caraṇāyudha), śāli rice, milk, decoction enema (nirūha) and sexual intercourse are recommended.
notes: caraṇāyudha, literally "having the feet as weapons", is the usual word for the cock; commentators take it as cock-meat. śāli: a class of rice; its identification with particular varieties of Oryza sativa is probable. śastam is singular in the text.
lines_deva: शालिः पयो निरूहश्च शस्तं मैथुनमेव च
lines_iast: śāliḥ payo nirūhaśca śastaṃ maithunameva ca

hindi: वात के वेग को रोकने से मल, मूत्र और वात का रुकना, आध्मान, वेदना, क्लम और उदर में वात से उत्पन्न होने वाले अन्य रोग होते हैं।
english: Retention of faeces, urine and flatus, distension, pain, exhaustion and other diseases born of Vāta in the abdomen would arise from suppression of flatus (vāta).

text_flags.why: The compound is vāta-ja ("born of Vāta"); the long ā in vātājāḥ has no grammatical basis; probable typing slip.

notes: vāta in viṇmūtravāta and vātanigraha is flatus; vātaja refers to Vāta as doṣa. jaṭhare can also be read with the preceding symptoms ("in the abdomen").

hindi: वहाँ स्नेहन और स्वेदन की विधि, वर्तियाँ, भोजन, पान, बस्तियाँ और वातानुलोमन प्रशस्त हैं।
english: There, the procedure of oleation and sweating, suppositories (varti), foods, drinks, enemas and whatever moves Vāta downward (vātānulomana) are recommended.
notes: vātānulomana: making Vāta move in its normal downward direction. It can be read as a separate item or as qualifying the foods and drinks ("foods ... that move Vāta downward").

words.gloss: itching, rashes, loss of taste, facial blemishes, swelling, pallor disease, fevers

hindi: छर्दि के वेग को रोकने से कण्डू, कोठ, अरुचि, व्यंग, शोथ, पाण्डुरोग, ज्वर, कुष्ठ, हृल्लास और वीसर्प रोग होते हैं।
english: Itching (kaṇḍū), rashes (koṭha), loss of taste (aruci), facial blemishes (vyaṅga), swelling (śotha), pallor disease (pāṇḍu), fever (jvara), kuṣṭha, nausea (hṛllāsa) and spreading inflammation (vīsarpa) are diseases born of suppressing vomiting.
notes: pāṇḍvāmaya is taken as one item (pāṇḍu-roga). Modern equivalents: koṭha urticaria-like wheals (probable); vyaṅga facial hyperpigmentation, melasma-like (probable); pāṇḍu anaemia (standard); kuṣṭha a group of skin diseases incl. but not only leprosy (standard); vīsarpa erysipelas-like spreading lesions (probable).

hindi: यहाँ भोजन करके प्रच्छर्दन, धूम, लंघन, रक्तमोक्षण, रूक्ष अन्नपान, व्यायाम और विरेक प्रशस्त हैं।
english: Here, emesis after eating, medicated smoking (dhūma), lightening (laṅghana), bloodletting, dry food and drink, exercise and purgation are recommended.
notes: bhuktvā goes with pracchardanam (emesis induced after a meal). laṅghana: lightening therapy, including fasting. śasyate is singular in the text.

hindi: छींक के वेग को रोकने से मन्यास्तम्भ, शिरःशूल, अर्दित, अर्धावभेदक और इन्द्रियों की दुर्बलता होती है।
english: Stiffness of the neck (manyāstambha), headache, ardita and ardhāvabhedaka, and weakness of the senses would arise from suppression of sneezing.
notes: manyā: the sides or back of the neck. ardita: facial paralysis (standard). ardhāvabhedaka: pain in one half of the head, hemicrania, compared with migraine (probable).

words.gloss: in the region above the clavicles

hindi: वहाँ जत्रु के ऊपर के भाग में अभ्यंग, स्वेद, नावन के साथ धूम, वातनाशक भोज्य और भोजन के पश्चात् लिया जाने वाला घृत हितकर हैं।
english: There, oil massage of the region above the clavicles, sweating, medicated smoking together with nasal therapy (nāvana), Vāta-destroying food and ghee taken after meals are beneficial.

text_flags.why: The printed ādhyaṃ has dh; ādya ("food", from √ad) is the expected word; probable typing slip.

notes: ūrdhvajatru: the part of the body above the clavicles (head and neck). ādya taken as "food"; it could also be read as an adjective qualifying ghṛtam. hitam is singular in the text.

hindi: डकार के वेग को रोकने से हिक्का, श्वास, अरुचि, कम्प और हृदय तथा छाती में विबन्ध होते हैं; वहाँ हिक्का के समान औषध है।
english: Hiccup, dyspnoea (śvāsa), loss of taste, tremor and constriction of the heart and chest arise from suppression of belching; there the medicine is the same as for hiccup.
notes: The verse has no verb in the first line; "arise" supplies the copula. hikkāyāḥ tulyam: the same treatment as prescribed for hikkā.

hindi: जम्भाई के वेग को रोकने से विनाम, आक्षेप, संकोच, सुप्ति, कम्प और प्रवेपन होते हैं; वहाँ सब वातनाशक औषध।
english: Bending (vināma), convulsions, contractions, numbness, tremor and shaking arise from suppression of yawning; there, all Vāta-destroying medicine.
notes: The second line is verbless; the treatment is simply stated ("all Vāta-destroying medicine"). kampa and pravepana are near-synonyms (tremor, violent shaking).

words.gloss: from suppression of the urge of hunger

hindi: भूख के वेग को रोकने से कृशता, दुर्बलता, विवर्णता, अंगमर्द, अरुचि और भ्रम होते हैं; वहाँ स्निग्ध, उष्ण और लघु भोजन।
english: Emaciation, weakness, discoloration, body-ache, loss of taste and giddiness arise from suppression of the urge of hunger; there, unctuous, hot and light food.

text_flags.why: Two typing slips: kārśay for kārśya ("emaciation") and aṅamarda for aṅgamarda ("body-ache", as in 7.10 and 7.23); the corrected line has 16 syllables.

notes: The second line is verbless.

hindi: प्यास के वेग को रोकने से कण्ठ और मुख का सूखना, बहरापन, श्रम, साद और हृदय में व्यथा होते हैं; वहाँ शीतल तर्पण अभीष्ट है।
english: Dryness of the throat and mouth, deafness, fatigue, lassitude (sāda) and distress in the heart arise from suppression of thirst; there a cold refreshing nourishment (tarpaṇa) is prescribed.
notes: tarpaṇa: a satisfying, nourishing preparation (often a drink or gruel); the verse does not specify. iṣyate literally "is desired".
lines_deva: कण्ठास्यशोषो बाधिर्यं श्रमः सादो हृदि व्यथा
lines_iast: kaṇṭhāsyaśoṣo bādhiryaṃ śramaḥ sādo hṛdi vyathā

hindi: आँसुओं के वेग को रोकने से प्रतिश्याय, नेत्ररोग, हृद्रोग, अरुचि और भ्रम होते हैं; वहाँ निद्रा, मद्य और प्रिय कथाएँ।
english: Coryza (pratiśyāya), eye disease, heart disease, loss of taste and giddiness arise from suppression of tears; there, sleep, wine and pleasant talk.

text_flags.why: The word is bāṣpa ("tears"), as printed in 7.4; the short a here is a probable typing slip.

notes: The second line is verbless. kathāḥ: pleasant conversation or stories.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. (list compound; dvandva sense, singular as printed)

hindi: निद्रा के वेग को रोकने से जम्भाई, अंगमर्द, तन्द्रा, शिरोरोग और आँखों में भारीपन होते हैं; वहाँ नींद और संवाहन।
english: Yawning, body-ache, drowsiness (tandrā), disease of the head and heaviness of the eyes arise from suppression of sleep; there, sleep and massages (saṃvāhana).
notes: The second line is verbless. saṃvāhana: gentle pressing or stroking massage of the limbs.

words.gloss: from suppression of breathing due to exertion

hindi: श्रम से होने वाले श्वास के वेग को रोकने से गुल्म, हृद्रोग और सम्मोह उत्पन्न होते हैं; वहाँ विश्राम और वातनाशक क्रियाएँ हितकर हैं।
english: Gulma, heart disease and fainting (saṃmoha) arise from suppression of breathing due to exertion; there, rest and Vāta-destroying measures are beneficial.

text_flags.why: The compound needs hṛd-roga ("heart disease", as in 7.22); the d is missing; probable typing slip.
vāta-ghnī (f. of vāta-ghna, "Vāta-destroying") agrees with kriyāḥ; dh for gh is a probable typing slip.

notes: gulma kept as Sanskrit: a lump or mass in the abdomen (standard: abdominal mass/tumour-like swelling). saṃmoha: loss of consciousness or stupor.
lines_deva: जायन्ते तत्र विश्रामो वातध्न्यश्च क्रिया हिताः
lines_iast: jāyante tatra viśrāmo vātadhnyaśca kriyā hitāḥ

hindi: वेगों के रोकने से उत्पन्न होने वाले जो ये रोग कहे गए हैं, उनकी उत्पत्ति न हो ऐसा चाहने वाला इन वेगों को न रोके।
english: Wishing that these diseases born of the suppression of urges, which have been described, should not arise, one should not suppress these urges.

text_flags.why: The sense requires vega-nigraha-ja ("born of suppressing urges"); vegā- with long ā is a possible typing slip (reading vega-anigraha would give the opposite sense). The metre is unaffected.

words.gloss: of acts of mind, speech and body

hindi: किन्तु जो इस लोक और परलोक में अपना हित चाहता है, वह मन, वाणी और शरीर के साहसपूर्ण और निन्दित कर्मों के इन वेगों को रोके।
english: But one who seeks his good after death and here should restrain these urges: those of rash and censured acts of mind, speech and body.

text_flags.why: aścastānām is not a word; a-śasta ("censured, not praised") gives the sense and the metre; probable typing slip.

notes: sāhasa can also be taken as a noun ("rash deeds") in apposition to the karmans. The list of urges to be restrained continues in 7.27 to 7.29.
lines_deva: इमांस्तु धारयेद्वेगान् हितार्थी प्रेत्य चेह च
lines_iast: imāṃstu dhārayedvegān hitārthī pretya ceha ca

words.gloss: urges of greed, grief, fear, anger, pride

hindi: बुद्धिमान् व्यक्ति लोभ, शोक, भय, क्रोध और मान के वेगों को तथा निर्लज्जता, ईर्ष्या, अतिराग और अभिध्या के वेगों को रोके।
english: The intelligent one should restrain the urges of greed, grief, fear, anger and pride, and of shamelessness, envy, excessive passion and covetousness (abhidhyā).
notes: The genitives of the second line depend on vegān of the first. māna: pride or conceit. abhidhyā: longing for another's property.

hindi: कठोर, अत्यधिक, चुगली करने वाले, असत्य और असमय कहे गए वचन के उठे हुए वेग को रोके।
english: One should restrain the urge, once it has arisen, toward speech that is harsh, excessive, slanderous, untrue or untimely.

text_flags.why: Printed puruṣāssya ("man") makes no sense with the genitives qualifying vākyasya; paruṣasya ("harsh") is required by the sense and keeps 8 syllables; probable misreading of the scan. The doubled s (ssy) is also irregular.

notes: sūcaka: tale-bearing, slandering.

words.gloss: such as enjoyment of women, theft, violence

hindi: जो कोई भी शारीरिक प्रवृत्ति दूसरों को पीड़ा देने वाली होती है, जैसे स्त्री-भोग, चोरी, हिंसा आदि, उसके वेगों को रोके।
english: Whatever bodily activity there is that involves harm to others, such as enjoyment of women, theft, violence and the like, one should restrain its urges.
notes: strībhoga is unqualified in the text; commentators take it as intercourse with another's wife or forbidden women. Rendered as printed.

words.gloss: of acts of mind, speech and body

hindi: मन, वाणी और शरीर के कर्मों के निष्पाप होने से पुण्यकीर्ति वाला सुखी पुरुष धर्म, अर्थ और काम का भोग करता है और उनका संचय करता है।
english: Because his acts of mind, speech and body are free of sin, a man of good repute, happy, enjoys and accumulates dharma, artha (wealth) and kāma (pleasure).
notes: puṇyaśabda: "having a virtuous name", i.e. well spoken of.
lines_deva: धर्मार्थकामान् पुरुषः सुखी भुङ्क्ते चिनोति च
lines_iast: dharmārthakāmān puruṣaḥ sukhī bhuṅkte cinoti ca

hindi: जो शारीरिक चेष्टा स्थिरता के लिए और बल बढ़ाने वाली होती है, वह शारीरिक व्यायाम कहलाती है; उसे मात्रा के अनुसार करना चाहिए।
english: Bodily activity which is aimed at steadiness and increases strength is known as bodily exercise (vyāyāma); one should practise it in due measure.
notes: yā ceṣṭā may also be split yā ca iṣṭā ("which is also desired / agreeable"). The repeated ceṣṭā is not rendered twice.

hindi: व्यायाम से हल्कापन, कार्य करने की सामर्थ्य, स्थिरता, दुःख सहने की क्षमता, दोषों का क्षय और अग्नि की वृद्धि होती है।
english: Lightness, capacity for work, steadiness, tolerance of hardship, reduction of the doṣas and increase of the digestive fire (agni) arise from exercise.
notes: doṣakṣaya: commentators take it as reduction of excess (especially Kapha); the text says only "reduction of doṣa".

hindi: अति व्यायाम से श्रम, क्लम, क्षय, तृष्णा, रक्तपित्त, प्रतामक, कास, ज्वर और छर्दि उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: Fatigue, exhaustion, wasting, thirst, raktapitta, pratāmaka, cough, fever and vomiting arise from excessive exercise.
notes: raktapitta: bleeding disorder, haemorrhage from body orifices (standard). pratāmaka: a variety of dyspnoea (tamaka-śvāsa with fainting); the long ā here fits the even-line cadence, so no flag. jāyate is singular in the text.

hindi: पसीना आना, श्वास की वृद्धि, अंगों का हल्कापन तथा हृदय आदि का उपरोध — यह व्यायाम का लक्षण है।
english: Onset of sweating, increase of breathing, lightness of the limbs, and obstruction of the heart and so on: this is the sign of exercise.
notes: The edition prints these two lines in round brackets with their own dandas and no verse number, probably marking them as an addition (the edition does not state the reason). hṛdayādyuparodha: a feeling of pressure in the heart region and other parts; commentators read the verse as the signs of exercise done to the proper limit.

words.gloss: exercise, laughter, talk, walking, sexual intercourse, night-waking

hindi: बुद्धिमान् व्यक्ति व्यायाम, हँसी, भाषण, मार्ग-गमन, ग्राम्यधर्म और रात्रि-जागरण का, अभ्यस्त होने पर भी, अति मात्रा में सेवन न करे।
english: The intelligent one should not indulge excessively in exercise, laughter, talking, travelling on foot (adhvan), sexual intercourse (grāmyadharma) and staying awake at night, even when accustomed to them.
notes: grāmyadharma, literally "village practice", is the usual term for sexual intercourse. adhvan: road, journey on foot.

words.gram: pres. part. m. nom. sg. ā-√kṛṣ

hindi: जो इनका तथा इस प्रकार के अन्यों का अतिमात्रा में सेवन करता है, वह हाथी को खींचते हुए सिंह के समान सहसा नष्ट हो जाता है।
english: He who practises these and others of this kind beyond measure suddenly perishes, like a lion dragging an elephant.
notes: 'etān' (m. acc. pl.) refers back to the excesses listed in the preceding verses of the chapter; the noun is not repeated here.
lines_deva: गजं सिंह इवाकर्षन् सहसा स विनश्यते
lines_iast: gajaṃ siṃha ivākarṣan sahasā sa vinaśyate

words.gloss: by excess of sexual intercourse, load-bearing, travel and work
words.gram: n. inst. pl. dvandva with ati-
ppp. m. nom. pl. ati-√kṛś caus.

words.gloss: by anger, grief, fear and exertion

hindi: जो अतिव्यवाय, भार, मार्ग-गमन और कर्म से अत्यन्त कृश हो गए हैं, और जो मनुष्य क्रोध, शोक, भय तथा आयास से आक्रान्त हैं,
english: Those who are greatly emaciated by excess of sexual intercourse, load-bearing, travel and work, and those men too who are overcome by anger, grief, fear and exertion,
notes: The edition prints this verse and the next in round brackets with no verse number, as in 33.1 (the edition does not state why). Line a has an opening bracket but no closing danda or bracket; line b ends '||)'. The sentence continues into 35.2, where the main verb (varjayeyuḥ) stands. 'ati-' may govern only vyavāya or the whole compound; the rendering takes it with the whole list.

words.gloss: children, the old and the windy (pravāta)

hindi: बालक, वृद्ध, प्रवात, और जो ऊँचे स्वर से बहुत बोलने वाले हैं, तथा जो भूखे और प्यासे हैं — वे व्यायाम का वर्जन करें।
english: children, the old, the windy (pravāta), those who talk much and loudly, and those who are hungry and thirsty: they should avoid exercise.
notes: Bracketed like 35.1, whose subjects it completes. 'pravāta' literally 'windy' / 'exposed to wind'; here it may mean persons in whom Vāta predominates or persons exposed to wind: the text does not decide.

hindi: बुद्धिमान् मनुष्य अभ्यस्त अहित से क्रमशः विरत हो, और हित का क्रम से सेवन करे; और यहाँ वह क्रम बताया जाता है।
english: A wise man should gradually desist from the unwholesome to which he is habituated, and should take up the wholesome gradually; and the sequence is taught here.

words.gloss: by those two (in respect of them)

hindi: उन दोनों के प्रक्षेप और अपचय में क्रम पाद-अंश का होना चाहिए; और उसके पश्चात् एकान्तर, फिर द्व्यन्तर तथा त्र्यन्तर।
english: In the adding and reducing of those two (the unwholesome and the wholesome), the sequence should be by quarter-parts; and then, after that, with an interval of one, then of two, and likewise of three.
notes: 'tābhyām' refers to the habitual unwholesome and the wholesome of verse 36; the bracketed words in the English name them. The text does not say what unit the intervals (antara) are counted in.

hindi: क्रम से घटाए गए दोष और क्रम से बढ़ाए गए गुण, ऐसे होकर, अपुनर्भाव को प्राप्त होते हैं और अप्रकम्प्य हो जाते हैं।
english: Doṣas (faults) reduced gradually and good qualities increased gradually, being so, go to non-recurrence and become unshakable.
notes: The two predicates are most naturally distributive (the reduced doṣas do not recur; the increased guṇas become unshakable), but the Sanskrit sets both after both subjects; the translation keeps that order. Here 'doṣa' means faults (the unwholesome habits of 36), not necessarily the three bodily doṣas.

words.gloss: with balanced Pitta, Vāta (anila) and Kapha

hindi: कुछ मनुष्य गर्भ से ही सम पित्त, अनिल और कफ वाले होते हैं; कुछ वातल, कुछ पित्तल तथा श्लेष्मल दिखाई देते हैं।
english: Some men, from conception onward, have Pitta, Vāta (anila) and Kapha in balance; some are seen to be Vāta-predominant (vātala), some Pitta-predominant (pittala), and likewise Kapha-predominant (śleṣmala).
notes: 'kecit' is printed once in line a and once in line b; 'dṛśyante' governs both lines.

hindi: उनमें पहले वाले अनातुर हैं, वातल आदि सदा आतुर रहते हैं; क्योंकि इनकी देहप्रकृति दोषानुशयिता कही जाती है।
english: Of them, the former are not sick; the Vāta-predominant and the rest are always sick; for their bodily constitution is called 'following of the doṣas' (doṣānuśayitā).
notes: 'pūrve' = those of balanced doṣas named first in 39. 'doṣānuśayitā' (the state of lying along with / being shaped by the doṣa) is kept as the Sanskrit term; the exact sense of -anuśayitā is not explained in the text.

words.gloss: of the regimen of the healthy
having all tastes in equal measure

hindi: उनके लिए स्वस्थवृत्त का विपरीत गुणों वाला विधान हितकर है; समधातु वाले के लिए सब रसों में सम सात्म्य प्रशस्त है।
english: For them, a rule of the regimen of the healthy (svasthavṛtta) of opposite qualities is wholesome; for one of balanced dhātus, suitability (sātmya) with all tastes in equal measure is praised.

text_flags.why: gen. sg. of samadhātu needs final visarga before pr-; the printed form looks like a dropped ḥ (possible typo).

notes: 'viparītaguṇaḥ' agrees with 'vidhiḥ': a regimen whose qualities are opposite to the predominant doṣa.

hindi: दो नीचे और सात सिर में स्थित ख और स्वेदमुख — ये मलायन दूषित तथा मात्रा से अधिक मलों द्वारा पीड़ित होते हैं।
english: The orifices, two below and seven in the head, and the openings of sweat: these channels of waste (malāyana) are afflicted by wastes that are vitiated and exceed their measure.
notes: 'dve' (n. du.) is printed before a vowel without sandhi, as dual -e requires (pragṛhya).
lines_deva: द्वे अधः सप्त शिरसि खानि स्वेदमुखानि च
lines_iast: dve adhaḥ sapta śirasi khāni svedamukhāni ca

hindi: मलायनों के भारीपन से मलवृद्धि को, हल्केपन से मलसंक्षय को, और अत्यधिक सङ्ग या उत्सर्ग से भी जाने।
english: One should know increase of waste from the heaviness of the channels of waste, depletion of waste from their lightness, and also from excessive obstruction or discharge.

text_flags.why: probable typo: the sense needs 'increase' (vṛddhi), contrasted with saṃkṣaya 'depletion'; 'malabuddhi' ('notion of waste') gives no fit sense. The split uses the corrected form.

notes: 'atīva' is taken with saṅgotsargāt ('excessive obstruction or discharge'). 'One should know' is a modal rendering of the optative; the object of 'also' is the increase and depletion just named.

words.gloss: by the signs of the doṣas
with opposites of disease and cause
words.gram: m. inst. pl. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
pres. part. caus. m. nom. sg. vi-√car

hindi: उन व्याधियों को दोषों के लिङ्गों से निर्धारित करके, मात्रा और काल का विचार करते हुए, साध्य व्याधियों की व्याधि और हेतु के प्रतिद्वन्द्वियों से चिकित्सा करे।
english: Having determined those diseases by the signs of the doṣas, one should treat the curable ones with what is opposed to the disease and its cause, considering measure and time.

text_flags.why: pratidvandva 'opposite' has -ndv-; '-ndhv-' looks like a typo.
possible typo: no word 'tvicārayan'; 'tu vicārayan' would add a syllable (17 in the half-verse), while 'vicārayan' gives 16. Split taken as 'vicārayan'.

words.gloss: of those whose regimen of the healthy is irregular
devoted to the regimen of the healthy

hindi: जिनका स्वस्थवृत्त विषम है, उन अनातुरों में ये तथा अन्य रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं; इसलिए स्वस्थवृत्त में तत्पर रहे।
english: For those who are not sick but whose regimen of the healthy (svasthavṛtta) is irregular, these and other diseases arise; therefore one should be devoted to the regimen of the healthy.
notes: 'anāturāḥ' is nom. pl. where a genitive agreeing with viṣamasvasthavṛttānām would be expected; it is taken with that genitive ('those not sick'). It could also be read with what follows ('the not-sick should therefore be devoted...'), but 'bhavet' is singular.

hindi: माधव-प्रथम मास में, फिर नभस्य-प्रथम में, और सहस्य-प्रथम में दोषसंचय को निकलवाए।
english: In the month that is first of Mādhava, again in the first of Nabhasya, and in the first of Sahasya, one should have the accumulation of doṣas removed.

text_flags.why: The month name is Mādhava; 'mādhva-' is not a word and gives only 15 syllables in the half-verse, 'mādhava-' gives 16.

notes: Mādhava, Nabhasya and Sahasya are month names. The compounds 'X-prathama' are ambiguous: 'the month first of (i.e. before) X' or 'the first part of X'; the text does not decide, so the translation stays literal. 'caiva': eva left untranslated as a mere particle.

words.gloss: of those whose bodies are oleated and sweated

hindi: जिनके शरीर स्निग्ध और स्विन्न हैं, उनका दोषसंचय नियमित रूप से ऊर्ध्व और अधः निकलवाए; तब बुद्धिमान् बस्तिकर्म और नस्यकर्म करे।
english: For those whose bodies have been oleated and sweated, (removal) upward and downward, regularly; then the wise one should perform enema therapy (bastikarma) and nasal therapy (nasyakarma).
notes: Line a has no verb of its own; it continues 'hārayet' of 46. The bracketed '(removal)' in English marks that carried-over sense; the Hindi likewise brings in दोषसंचय from 46.

hindi: इसके पश्चात् काल को जानने वाला क्रम के अनुसार और योग्यता के अनुसार सिद्ध रसायनों और वृष्य योगों का प्रयोग करे।
english: After this, the knower of time should employ, in due order and as suitable, proven rejuvenatives (rasāyana) and aphrodisiac applications (yoga).

text_flags.why: '-āsṃś-' is not a possible sandhi; acc. pl. yogān + ca gives yogāṃś ca. Typing slip.

hindi: इस प्रकार धातुओं के प्रकृतिस्थ रहने पर रोग उत्पन्न नहीं होते, धातु बढ़ते हैं और जरा मन्दता को प्राप्त होती है।
english: Thus, the dhātus remaining in their natural state, diseases do not arise; the dhātus grow, and old age reaches slowness.

words.gram: ppp. m. nom. sg. caus. ni-√dṛś

hindi: यह विधि निज विकारों की अनुत्पत्ति के लिए दिखाई गई है; अन्यों की तो अलग से ही बताई जाएगी।
english: This method has been shown for the non-arising of endogenous (nija) disorders; that of the others will be taught separately.
notes: 'upadekṣyate' is a future form used passively ('will be taught'); the rendering 'that of the others' supplies the subject vidhiḥ from line a.

words.gloss: arising from bhūtas, poison, wind, fire, assault and the like

hindi: मनुष्यों के जो आगन्तु रोग भूत, विष, वायु, अग्नि, संप्रहार आदि से उत्पन्न होते हैं, उनमें प्रज्ञा का अपराध होता है।
english: In the exogenous (āgantu) diseases of men that arise from bhūtas, poison, wind, fire, assault and the like, the intellect (prajñā) errs.
notes: 'bhūta' may mean spirits/beings or living creatures; kept as bhūta. 'vāyu' here is the external wind listed among outer causes, so rendered 'wind', not the doṣa.

words.gloss: envy, grief, fear, anger, pride, hatred and the like
born of the offence of intellect

hindi: और जो ईर्ष्या, शोक, भय, क्रोध, मान, द्वेष आदि मनोविकार हैं, वे भी सब प्रज्ञापराध से उत्पन्न कहे गए हैं।
english: And the mental disorders, envy, grief, fear, anger, pride, hatred and the like, are also all said to be born of the offence of intellect (prajñāparādha).

words.gloss: knowledge of place, time and self

hindi: प्रज्ञापराधों का त्याग, इन्द्रियों का उपशम, स्मृति, देश, काल और आत्मा का विज्ञान, तथा सद्वृत्त का अनुवर्तन —
english: Giving up of offences of intellect, calming of the senses, memory, knowledge of place, time and self, and following of good conduct (sadvṛtta):
notes: A list of subjects; the sentence closes in 54 ('eṣa mārgo nidarśitaḥ').

words.gram: ppp. m. nom. sg. caus. ni-√dṛś

hindi: — यह मार्ग आगन्तुओं की अनुत्पत्ति के लिए दिखाया गया है। प्राज्ञ पहले ही वह करे जिसे वह अपने लिए हितकर जाने।
english: this path has been shown for the non-arising of the exogenous (diseases). The wise one should do beforehand that which he would know to be wholesome for himself.
notes: Completes the list of 53. 'āgantūnām' stands alone; '(diseases)' is supplied from 51.

words.gloss: understanding of the teaching of the reliable

hindi: आप्तोपदेश का प्रज्ञान और प्रतिपत्ति विकारों की अनुत्पत्ति का और उत्पन्न विकारों की शान्ति का कारण है।
english: Understanding of the teaching of the reliable (āpta) and putting it into practice (pratipatti) are the cause for the non-arising of disorders and for the pacification of those that have arisen.
notes: 'pratipatti' may mean 'putting into practice' or 'right understanding'; the first fits the pairing with prajñāna.

words.gloss: of sinful conduct, speech and mind

hindi: पापी आचरण, वचन और सत्त्व वाले, चुगलखोर, कलहप्रिय, मर्म पर उपहास करने वाले, लोभी, दूसरों की वृद्धि से द्वेष करने वाले, शठ,
english: Those of sinful conduct, speech and mind (sattva), informers, lovers of quarrels, mockers at (others') weak points (marma), the greedy, haters of others' prosperity, the deceitful,
notes: A list of subjects; the predicate 'parivarjyāḥ' comes in 57. 'marma' literally 'vital spot'; here figurative.

words.gram: gerundive (kṛtya) m. nom. pl. pari-√vṛj caus.

hindi: दूसरों की निन्दा में रत, चपल, शत्रुओं का सेवन करने वाले, निर्दय, धर्म को त्यागे हुए — ये अधम मनुष्य परिवर्जनीय हैं।
english: those delighting in slandering others, the fickle, those who serve enemies, the pitiless, those who have abandoned dharma: these lowest of men are to be avoided.
notes: The token 'parāpavādaratayaścapalā' is printed without a space between two words (ratayaś capalāḥ); both come from that one token.

words.gloss: in intellect, learning, age, character, steadiness, memory and concentration

hindi: बुद्धि, विद्या, आयु, शील, धैर्य, स्मृति और समाधि में वृद्ध, वृद्धों की सेवा करने वाले, स्वभाव को जानने वाले, व्यथा से रहित,
english: Those advanced in intellect, learning, age, character, steadiness, memory and concentration, who attend on elders, who know the nature (of things), who are free from distress,
notes: A list of subjects; the predicate 'sevyāḥ' comes in 59. 'svabhāvajña' may mean knowing the nature of things or of people; the object is not stated.

words.gloss: whose hearing and sight are meritorious

hindi: सब प्राणियों के प्रति सुमुख, प्रशान्त, प्रशंसित व्रतों वाले, सन्मार्ग बताने वाले, जिनका श्रवण और दर्शन पुण्य है — ये सेव्य हैं।
english: kindly-faced to all beings, tranquil, of praised vows, teachers of the good path, whose hearing and sight are meritorious: these are to be resorted to.
notes: 'puṇyaśravaṇadarśanāḥ': hearing of them and seeing them is meritorious (bahuvrīhi); 'śaṃsitavrata' may also mean 'firm in vows'.

words.gloss: in the use of the wholesome

hindi: आहार, आचार और चेष्टा में, परलोक और इस लोक में सुख चाहने वाला बुद्धिमान् हित के सेवन में परम प्रयत्न करे।
english: In diet, conduct and activity, the wise one who desires happiness hereafter and here should make the highest effort in the use of the wholesome.

hindi: रात में दही न खाए, न घृत और शर्करा के बिना, न मुद्ग-यूष के बिना, न क्षौद्र के बिना, न उष्ण, न आमलकों के बिना।
english: One should not eat curd (dadhi) at night, nor without ghee and sugar, nor without mudga yūṣa, nor without honey, nor hot, nor without āmalaka fruits.
notes: Plant identifications: mudga = Vigna radiata, green gram (standard); āmalaka = Phyllanthus emblica, Indian gooseberry (standard). 'nāmalakair' is split na + āmalakaiḥ (not na + amalakaiḥ).
lines_deva: न नक्तं दधि भुञ्जीत न चाप्यघृतशर्करम्
lines_iast: na naktaṃ dadhi bhuñjīta na cāpyaghṛtaśarkaram

words.gloss: fever, asṛkpitta, vīsarpa, kuṣṭha, the disease pāṇḍu and giddiness

hindi: विधि को छोड़कर दही का प्रेमी ज्वर, असृक्पित्त, वीसर्प, कुष्ठ, पाण्डु रोग, भ्रम और उग्र कामला को प्राप्त हो सकता है।
english: One fond of curd who abandons the rule may get fever, asṛkpitta, vīsarpa, kuṣṭha, the disease pāṇḍu, giddiness, and severe kāmalā.
notes: Disease names are kept in Sanskrit. 'asṛkpitta' is the same word as raktapitta (asṛk = blood). 'pāṇḍv-āmaya' read as 'the disease pāṇḍu'; 'āmaya' could also be taken with the whole list ('the diseases fever ...').

words.gram: gerundive (kṛtya) m. nom. pl. vi-√dhṛ caus.

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक: वेग, वेगों से उत्पन्न रोग और उनकी भेषज; जिनके वेग रोकने योग्य हैं, और किस प्रयोजन से; जो हित और अहित है;
english: Here, the verses: the urges, the diseases arising from urges and their medicine; whose urges are to be suppressed, and for what purpose; what is wholesome and unwholesome;
notes: 'tatra ślokāḥ' introduces the chapter's summary verses (63–66), one running list of topics whose predicate 'sarvam evāvadan muniḥ' comes in 66. The lead-in stands outside the metre. 'teṣām' may refer to the urges or to the diseases.

words.gloss: medicine for the diseases of the channels of waste

hindi: अभ्यस्त अहित जो वर्ज्य है, और अनभ्यस्त जो सेव्य है, उनके विषय में क्रम; प्रकृति के अनुसार आहार; और मलायनों के रोगों की औषध;
english: the sequence regarding the habitual unwholesome that is to be avoided and the unaccustomed that is to be used; diet according to constitution (prakṛti); the medicine for diseases of the channels of waste;
lines_deva: उचिते चाहिते वर्ज्ये सेव्ये चानुचिते क्रमः
lines_iast: ucite cāhite varjye sevye cānucite kramaḥ

hindi: भविष्य में होने वाले रोगों की अनुत्पत्ति के लिए जो औषध है; और अपने सुख के इच्छुक बुद्धिमान् द्वारा वर्जनीय और सेवनीय पुरुष;
english: the medicine which is for the non-arising of future diseases; the persons to be avoided and to be resorted to by the wise one who desires his own happiness;

words.gram: n. loc. sg. (title, in apposition to adhyāye)

hindi: और जिस विधि से और जिस कारण दही सेव्य है — वह सब अत्रिज मुनि ने नवेगान्धारण अध्याय में कहा।
english: and by which rule and why curd is to be eaten: all this the Atri-born sage told in the chapter 'Na vegān dhāraṇa' (not holding back the urges).
notes: 'atrijaḥ' (born of Atri) is an epithet; the line does not name the sage. 'tat ... sarvam' sums up the list begun in 63. The chapter title is the opening words 'na vegān dhāraṇa-' kept as a single name.
lines_deva: विधिना दधि सेव्यं च येन यस्मात्तदत्रिजः
lines_iast: vidhinā dadhi sevyaṃ ca yena yasmāttadatrijaḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में नवेगान्धारणीय नामक सातवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna), the seventh chapter, named Navegāndhāraṇīya (On not holding back the urges).

text_flags.why: nom. sg. of adhyāya is adhyāyaḥ, agreeing with saptamaḥ; the long -āḥ (nom. pl.) looks like a typo.

notes: Colophon. The Sanskrit has no verb; the translation keeps it verbless. Ślokasthāna is the name this edition uses for the first section.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने नवेगान्धारणीयो नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायाः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne navegāndhāraṇīyo nāma saptamo'dhyāyāḥ
